newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Forint eases vs dlr, record forex futures trade.
newsitem.headline: Forint eases vs dlr, record forex futures trade.

text.p: Hungary's forint closed slightly easier on Friday in very light turnover while soaring end-of-year currency futures turnover on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) smashed the previous record by over 50 percent.
The forint ended at 161.45/55 to one dollar, compared with its opening of 161.40, dealers said.
"It was a very quiet day," said Noemi Koppendorfer of Magyar Hitel Bank. "Brokers were just covering customer deals."
The unit closed some 30 pips weaker than the central bank resistance level.
Koppendorfer said that although Hungary's markets would be open next week, she did not expect trade to liven up before the end of the holiday period on January 6.
Both the money and equities exchanges will trade on Monday, December 30th.
Hectic end-of-year trade on the BCE currency futures market resulted in record turnover of 26 billion forints, well above the previous peak set earlier this month of 16.4 billion.
The Ecu and sterling were the most popular currencies, especially for September 1997 contracts, for which sterling falls approached the three-forint maximum permitted.
